sources.title: Our History: Bahawalpur
sources.note: Punjab government account distinguishing city and former princely state, its eighteenth-century roots, 1802 phase, and later continuity.

sources.title: Derawar and the Desert Forts of Cholistan
sources.note: UNESCO-hosted Pakistan nomination on desert geography, fort network, caravan routes, scarce water, and the 1804 recovery.

sources.title: The History of Bahawalpur, 1848 public-domain scan
sources.note: Shahamet Ali history abridged from Bahawalpur family annals, with exact events and later direct observations clearly separated.

sources.title: The History of Bahawalpur, Oxford digitization
sources.note: Oxford digitization of Shahamet Ali used for bounded later observations on food, dress, education, work, and evidentiary silence.

sources.title: Power Relations and the Changing Orientalist Discourse regarding Nawabs of Bahawalpur
sources.note: Peer-reviewed critique of colonial descriptions, the 1808 mission, state geography, plural administration, and the 1815 protection request.

sources.title: Insurgencies and invasions faced by Bahawalpur under Bahawal Khan II
sources.note: Academic study of rebellions, fort campaigns, the 1802 title and mint, and state military responses under Bahawal Khan II.

sources.title: The Architect-Viziers of Bahawalpur State
sources.note: Islamia University study of the 1809 to 1836 vizierate, offices, diplomacy, military organization, irrigation, and structural vulnerability.

sources.title: Mountstuart Elphinstone papers
sources.note: British Library catalogue for the 1808 to 1809 Afghan embassy archive, including mission journals, papers, and reports.

sources.title: Mountstuart Elphinstone
sources.note: Encyclopaedia Iranica account of the 1808 mission, its geopolitical purpose, Shah Shuja negotiations, and 1809 treaty.

sources.title: An Account of the Kingdom of Caubul, 1815
sources.note: Library of Congress digitization of Elphinstone's mission narrative, used for the exact Bahawalpur journey and elite hospitality.

sources.title: Murad's travels: courtesanly mobility, honour, and defiance in late eighteenth-century Multan
sources.note: Cambridge study of a gendered travel narrative and Bahawalpur courtiers Suba Rai and Daulat Rai in a regional literary network.

sources.title: Derawar through the Ages: A Military and Dynastic History
sources.note: University of Peshawar archaeology journal study of Derawar as fort, capital, refuge, treasure site, and caravan crossroads.

sources.title: Derawar Fort
sources.note: Pakistan Department of Archaeology and Museums monument record for the fort and its historical setting.

sources.title: Tombs and mosque of Uch Sharif
sources.note: UNESCO-hosted Pakistan nomination describing five Uch monuments, their Sufi associations, brickwork, timber, tiles, painting, and spatial features.

sources.title: Mirat-i Daulat-i Abbasi, a rare historical source on Bahawalpur
sources.note: University of the Punjab Persian scholarship identifying the court-sponsored chronicle, its author, title, subject, and historical importance.

sources.title: Catalogue of the Persian Manuscripts in the British Museum, Or. 1631
sources.note: Public-domain catalogue entry giving manuscript extent, hands, script style, Bahawalpur completion place, and AH 1224 to 1227 dates.

sources.title: Religio-festive Trends of the People of Bahawalpur State, 1727 to 1947
sources.note: Pakistan Journal of History and Culture study of food, Muslim and Hindu communities, festivals, fairs, social contact, and source dates.

sources.title: Sairistan-i Mubaraz ud Daula as a cultural source
sources.note: University of the Punjab review of a Persian travelogue based on fourteen years of later observational residence in Bahawalpur.

sources.title: Civilization and Culture of Bahawalpur State: A Research Review
sources.note: Islamia University journal review of rural culture, crafts, hearth-centered gathering, pottery, textiles, embroidery, and natural remedies.

sources.title: Ethnomedicinal knowledge of indigenous plants of Cholistan
sources.note: Peer-reviewed modern field study of interviews and seventy medicinal plants, useful only as later evidence with an explicit date limit.

sources.title: Comparative ethnobotany of Cholistan and Pothwar
sources.note: Peer-reviewed modern interview study recording sixty-seven Cholistan medicinal plant species and warning that knowledge is disappearing.

sources.title: Zootherapy as traditional therapeutic strategy in Cholistan
sources.note: Peer-reviewed modern study of animal-derived remedies, cited as living practice evidence rather than proof of early nineteenth-century treatment.

sources.title: Common medicinal plants used by people of Cholistan Desert
sources.note: Medical journal survey of present traditional plant use and the need to conserve knowledge, with no claim of direct 1800 continuity.

sources.title: The Lifeline of Cholistan Desert
sources.note: Pakistan Council of Research in Water Resources profile of modern rainwater ponds, kunds, storage, and desert water infrastructure.

sources.title: PCRWR Annual Report 2023 to 2024
sources.note: Official account of current Cholistan rainwater dependence, toba capacity, water deficit, drought work, and quality assessment.

sources.title: Cholistan Drought Management Plan
sources.note: Punjab public-sector plan documenting present tobas, kunds, turbidity, disinfection gaps, shared livestock use, and rainfall dependence.

sources.title: To Assess the Trends of Living and Poverty in a Desert Climate
sources.note: Modern field survey of Cholistan water, livestock, temporary settlement, branch-and-leaf gopas, and inadequate sanitation, never back-projected.

sources.title: Sustainability of Subsistence Livelihoods of Agro-Pastoralists in Cholistan
sources.note: Peer-reviewed geography study of current nomadism, transhumance, settlements, farming, livestock, plants, water, households, and changing livelihoods.

sources.title: Launching of Primary Education in Bahawalpur State, 1866 to 1955
sources.note: Bibliographic record fixing organized state primary education to a later 1866 start, preventing projection into 1800 to 1815.

sources.title: Contribution of Bahawalpur scholars in Arabic prose
sources.note: Islamia University scholarship on Arabic learning, trade contacts, and later educational centers, used with chronological restraint.

sources.title: Bahawalpur printing and learning history
sources.note: Islamia University journal record dating the Sadiq al-Anwar press to 1866 and later Persian, English, and Urdu correspondence changes.

sources.title: Iqbāl Nāma-i Saadat Ayat manuscript study
sources.note: LUMS Bunyad record of another unpublished Persian political history, showing a later Bahawalpur manuscript tradition without backdating it.

sources.title: Agrarian economy of the princely state of Bahawalpur, 1866 to 1924
sources.note: University of the Punjab journal record for later agrarian research, used to separate later reforms from early canal evidence.

sources.title: District Census Report Bahawalnagar historical chapter
sources.note: Official census-history compilation on the 1802 mint, succession, lost districts, and later restoration, checked against closer sources.

sources.title: Bahawalpur one rupee coin, 1858
sources.note: British Museum object record for a later state coin, demonstrating monetary continuity while not dating its specimen to 1800.

sources.title: Google Books record for Bahawalpur State Gazetteer, 1904
sources.note: Bibliographic record for the official state gazetteer, a later synthesis whose evidence cannot automatically describe 1800 households.

sources.title: Bahawalpur: where the sands preserve a kingdom
sources.note: Associated Press of Pakistan feature synthesizing official archaeology on Derawar, state-building, water, routes, learning, and care.

proposedOverrides.name: Bahawalpur
proposedOverrides.summary: Historical Bahawalpur State; its 1815 Maratha replacement is a cartographic error.

batchIdentityNotes: Exact target is the historical Bahawalpur State id, not the present city described by the imported summary.
The sole six-position polygon is coarse and even excludes the sampled capital while including sampled Sukkur.
The 1800 shape directly reuses arcs with atlas Sikh, Rajput, and Sindh layers, which are technical seams rather than surveyed frontiers.
The 1815 replacement by an enormous Maratha layer is cartographic error; Bahawalpur continued.
